title: Stage 3: Rebase and squash for review
summary: 14:00. Your branch has five commits, two of them fixes to earlier ones. Shape it into a clean story before you request review.

steps.title: Briefing
body: b2 Show coupon field at checkout
e5 fixup! Show coupon field at checkout
You made c3 and e5 with `git commit --fixup=<hash>`, which writes the special subject `fixup! <target subject>`. Now:
Git pre-arranges the todo list: each `fixup!` commit moves directly under its target, with the verb `fixup`. You only need to decide what to do with `wip`.

steps.prompt: Write the todo list `git rebase -i --autosquash` opens, before you change anything (one line per commit, `verb hash subject`).
answer: fixup c3 fixup! Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)
pick b2 Show coupon field at checkout
fixup e5 fixup! Show coupon field at checkout
steps.explain: Each `fixup!` commit is moved right after the commit whose subject it names, and gets the verb `fixup`. Other commits keep their order.

steps.prompt: `d4 wip` contains a useful validation change for the coupon field. What is the best edit to the todo?
options: Move it under `b2` and change it to `fixup` (or `squash` if its message adds something)
steps.explain: Its change belongs to the coupon-field commit. Dropping would lose code; keeping *wip* leaves an unreviewable commit.

steps.prompt: After your edited rebase, how many commits does `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` print? (A number.)
code: fixup c3 fixup! Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)
pick b2 Show coupon field at checkout
fixup e5 fixup! Show coupon field at checkout
steps.explain: Two picks, everything else melted into them: one commit for the logic, one for the UI. Exactly the two-commit story a reviewer wants.

steps.prompt: Now that the branch is rewritten: fine or not?
items: Telling the reviewer you rewrote the branch
steps.explain: A plain push is rejected (the old tip is no longer an ancestor). `--force` would overwrite a reviewer's pushed suggestion without warning.

steps.title: Autosquash, fold the wip, update the PR
prompt: Your branch `feature/SHOP-142-coupons` in `~/shop` is pushed and looks like the briefing: two real commits, two `fixup!` commits and a `wip` commit with a useful validation change for the coupon field.
1. Rebase onto `origin/main` with `--autosquash`, and also turn `wip` into a `fixup` so it folds into `Show coupon field at checkout`.
2. Check what you changed against what reviewers saw: `git range-diff @{u}...HEAD`.
3. Update the pull request branch safely.
No editor opens here, so let `sed` edit the todo list: `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR="sed -i 's/^pick \(.*\) wip$/fixup \1 wip/'" git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main`.

checks.name: two commits for review
checks.expectOutput:
Show coupon field at checkout
Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)
checks.fail: The branch should have exactly the two real commits. Did `wip` get folded in?

checks.name: the files did not change, only the history
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse 'feature/SHOP-142-coupons^{tree}')" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/tip-tree)" && git show feature/SHOP-142-coupons~1:src/Coupon.cs | grep -q '1 to 100'
checks.fail: The branch tip must have the same files as before, and `Add percentage coupons` must contain its fixup.

checks.name: the pull request branch is updated
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git rev-parse feature/SHOP-142-coupons)" = "$(git rev-parse feature/SHOP-142-coupons)" && ! test -d .git/rebase-merge
checks.fail: Push with `git push --force-with-lease` once the rebase is finished.

hints: Plain `git rebase -i --autosquash` would put the `fixup!` commits in place but leave `pick ... wip`. The `sed` turns that line into `fixup`.
Autosquash places `wip` after the fixups of `Show coupon field`, so `fixup` folds it into that commit.
Afterwards `git range-diff @{u}...HEAD` compares the old and new series commit by commit; then `git push --force-with-lease`.
solution: GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR="sed -i 's/^pick \(.*\) wip$/fixup \1 wip/'" git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main
steps.explain: `git range-diff` is the review tool for rewritten branches: it pairs each new commit with its old version and shows only what changed between them, which is exactly what a reviewer asks after a force-push ("what did you change since my review?"). GitHub's "Compare" link after a force-push shows the same idea.
